title: Phased compatibility shims and coordinated comms runway for model variant sunset
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Summary:
We will retire the legacy model-variant family (v1.x) and migrate customers to the v2-compatible variants. To minimize churn, this ticket coordinates a phased approach that uses compatibility shims (API alias + SDK adapters), staged telemetry and warning surfaces, curated migration bundles, and tightly synchronized release notes / comms across Console, API docs, SDKs, and support playbooks.

Goals:
- Reduce developer friction by providing a drop-in compatibility layer for 90% of existing calls.
- Provide clear, minimal-migration paths for advanced users who need feature parity.
- Ensure no high-severity production regressions through automated evals and a canary rollout.
- Coordinate cross-team timing and messaging so customers see a single coherent narrative.

Approach and components:
1) Compatibility shim (server-side):
   - API alias route /v1-compat/* that translates v1 request shapes to v2 model and responses where possible.
   - Backstop: route-level feature-flag to disable shim in outages.
   - Telemetry: shim emits event shim_translation_version + regression_score sample per request.

2) SDK adapters (client-side):
   - Add an adapter layer to official SDKs that maps deprecated param names and provides runtime warnings.
   - Publish migration helpers: e.g., migrateParams(), linting rule for SDK consumers.

3) Migration bundles and examples:
   - Provide three migration bundles: Basic (no code changes), Medium (parameter rename + small prompt tweaks), Advanced (model-behavior tuning guidance).
   - Include runnable sample repos and a migration diagnostics script that compares outputs and token costs.

4) Release notes and comms playbook:
   - Single canonical release notes entry (Console + Docs + API changelog) with per-audience callouts: SDK users, self-hosted/private customers, Dedicated customers.
   - Weekly staged comms cadence: Early Notice (60d), Beta & migration tools (45d), Broad Notice + sunset date (30d), Final Reminder (7d).
   - Support kit: canned responses, KB article, migration checklist for CSMs.

5) Rollout and quality gates:
   - Canary cohort: 5% of traffic limited to low-risk tenants for 2 weeks.
   - Automated regression checks: Eval suite covering 120 prompt templates, latency/cost regression thresholds.
   - Manual review gates: PM + Eng + Design signoff after canary.

Owners & responsibilities:
- PM (Lena): overall coordinator, customer comms cadence, release notes copy approval.
- Eng (OWN: ENG-2891): shim implementation, telemetry, canary routing, rollback hooks.
- SDK (OWN: ENG-3128): adapter PRs, lint rules, publish packages.
- Design (DES-7643): Console banners, notice UI, migration checklist UX.
- Support/CS: onboarding of high-touch customers and playbook execution.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server-side shim routes deployed behind a feature flag and passing the canary regression suite.
- SDK adapter releases published for JS, Python, and Go with migration helper docs.
- Release notes and Console banners scheduled and approved in the content calendar.
- Migration diagnostics script available in the public sample repo with runnable examples.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Shim may mask behavioral regressions that impact semantics. Mitigation: require regression_score < 0.05 across the eval set before expanding traffic.
- Risk: Customers ignore warnings. Mitigation: staged UI banners and automated in-API deprecation warnings (response header + X-Deprecated-Warn).
- Risk: Dedicated/private upgrades with strict policies. Mitigation: dedicated runbook and extra lead time; coordinate with Enterprise AE owners.

Artifacts & links:
- Migration sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/migration-bundles/tree/PM-15642
- Draft release notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/PM-15642+-+Shim+and+Comms
- Canary dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/pm15642-canary

Next milestones:
- 2026-03-01: Engineering prototype for shim completed (done)
- 2026-03-12: SDK adapter alpha published (in progress)
- 2026-03-20: Internal canary start (scheduled)
- 2026-04-01: Broad notice to customers (planned)
- 2026-04-15: Sunset date for v1 variants (target)
